p.src: As the story continues, Baoyu was in Lin Daiyu's room telling the tale of the “rat-spirit” when Baochai happened in and mocked him for not knowing the allusion to “green wax” at the Lantern Festival. The three were trading barbs and laughing together. Baoyu had been afraid that Daiyu might indulge in a nap after eating, which could leave her food undigested, or keep her from sleeping that night—neither being good for her health. Fortunately Baochai's arrival and their cheerful talk dispelled Daiyu's drowsiness, and only then did he set his mind at ease. Suddenly they heard an uproar from his rooms. After everyone listened closely for a moment, Lin Daiyu was the first to laugh. “That is your nurse quarrelling with Xiren. Never mind Xiren; but if your nurse is seriously taking her to task again, the old woman must truly be losing her wits.”

p.src: Baoyu hastened to go over, but Baochai caught hold of him. “Above all, do not quarrel with your nurse,” she said. “She is old and muddleheaded, so the right thing is to yield to her.” “I know,” said Baoyu. With that, he went back and found Nanny Li standing in the middle of the room, leaning on her cane and berating Xiren. “You ungrateful little slut! I was the one who raised you to your present position, yet now when I come, you lie there on the kang as grand as you please and do not even acknowledge me. All you think of is making yourself into a little enchantress to bewitch Baoyu, until he ignores me and listens only to you girls. You are nothing but a raw little maid bought for a few miserable taels of silver. How dare you make mischief in this room! One of these days we shall drag you out and marry you off to some servant boy. Then we shall see whether you can go on bewitching Baoyu like a demon!” At first Xiren supposed that Nanny Li was angry only because she had been lying down, so she naturally tried to explain: “I am ill and had only just begun to perspire. My head was under the covers, so I truly did not see you come in,” and so forth. But when the old woman went on and on about her “bewitching Baoyu,” “playing the enchantress,” and being “married off to a servant boy,” shame and grievance overcame her, and she could not keep from crying.

p.src: Though Baoyu heard all this, there was little he could do. He could only explain that Xiren was ill and had taken medicine, adding, “If you do not believe me, ask the other maids.” This only made Nanny Li angrier. “You do nothing but protect that pack of vixens! How could you remember me now? Whom do you expect me to ask? Every one of them takes your side, and has not Xiren brought them all under her thumb? I know all about those goings-on. I shall go and tell the Old Lady and Her Ladyship about you. I nursed you until you were this big; but now that you no longer need my milk, you cast me aside and let these maids bully me as they please.” As she spoke, she too began to cry. By then Daiyu, Baochai, and the others had come over to mediate. “Dear Nanny,” they said, “if you would only make a little allowance for them, that would settle everything.” Seeing the two of them, Nanny Li caught hold of them and poured out her grievances, rambling endlessly about the tea Baoyu had drunk that day, Qianxue's dismissal, the cream from the previous day, and other such matters. As it happened, Xifeng had just finished reckoning the gambling accounts in the main apartments. Hearing the commotion at the back, she knew at once that Nanny Li's old complaint had flared up again and that she was berating Baoyu's attendants. She had lost money that day and was venting her anger on others. Xifeng hurried over, took Nanny Li by the arm, and said with a smile, “Dear Nanny, do not be angry. At this great festival the Old Lady has only just had one happy day. You are an elder, and when others raise their voices, you ought to restrain them. Surely you will not forget the rules yourself, make a din here, and upset the Old Lady? Just tell me who has behaved badly, and I shall beat her for you. There is piping-hot pheasant roasting at my place. Come quickly and have a drink with me.” As she spoke, she led her away and called out, “Feng'er, carry Granny Li's cane for her—and bring a handkerchief to wipe her tears.” Nanny Li was swept off her feet and followed Xifeng away, still protesting as she went: “I have no use for this old life of mine! Today I may as well cast all rules aside, make a great scene, and disgrace myself. Anything is better than enduring that little slut's insolence!” Baochai and Daiyu followed behind them. Seeing how Xifeng had managed matters, they clapped their hands and laughed. “Thank goodness that gust of wind came and whisked the old woman away!” Baoyu nodded and sighed. “Who knows where this score really came from? She only picks on those too gentle to resist. Yesterday, too, some girl must have offended her, and now she has charged it to Xiren's account.” Before he had finished, Qingwen laughed from beside him. “Who would be mad enough to offend her for no reason? And even if someone did offend her, she should have the courage to own up to it instead of dragging others into trouble!”

p.src: Still weeping, Xiren took Baoyu by the hand. “You have already offended an old nurse on my account, and now you are offending all these others because of me. Is that not enough for me to bear? Yet you insist on dragging someone else into it.” Seeing her so ill and now burdened with these fresh troubles, Baoyu hastily swallowed his anger and soothed her, persuading her to lie down again and sweat out her fever. Finding her as hot as burning coals, he stayed beside her, reclining nearby and urging her to think only of recovering and not upset herself over such trifles. Xiren gave a cold laugh. “If I became angry over such things, I could not remain in this room for a single moment. But if this goes on day after day and year after year, what is one to do? I am forever urging you not to offend people on our account. In the heat of the moment you think only of standing up for us, but they remember it all. Then, when some difficulty arises, whether their words sound fair or foul, what do you expect any of us to feel?” As she spoke, her tears began to flow despite herself; but fearing that Baoyu would be distressed, she forced them back once more.

p.src: Presently, an old maid-of-all-work brought in a freshly prepared second dose of medicine. Seeing that Xiren had only just begun to perspire, Baoyu would not let her rise. He carried the medicine to her bedside and gave it to her himself, then ordered the little maids to prepare the kang. Xiren said, “Whether you eat or not, you ought at least to sit awhile with the Old Lady and your mother, and amuse yourself with the young ladies before coming back. Then I can lie here quietly and rest for a while.” At this, Baoyu had no choice but to remove her hairpins and ornaments for her. Once he had seen her lie down, he went to the main apartments. After dining with Grandmother Jia, who still wished to relieve her boredom by playing cards with several elderly stewardesses, Baoyu remembered Xiren and returned to his room, where he found her sleeping fitfully. He thought of sleeping too, but it was still early. At that hour Qingwen, Qixia, Qiuwen, and Bihen had all gone in search of merriment with Yuanyang, Hupo, and the others. Only Sheyue remained, sitting beneath the lamp in the outer room, idly arranging dominoes. Baoyu asked with a smile, “Why didn’t you go and play with them?” “I have no money,” Sheyue replied. “There is such a heap of cash under the bed,” said Baoyu. “Isn’t that enough for you to lose?” Sheyue said, “If everyone goes off to play, who will be left in charge of this room? Besides, one of us is ill. There are lamps everywhere above and braziers below. Those old nurses have served us all day despite their age, so they deserve a rest; and the little maids have been attending us all day too—surely they ought to be allowed some amusement now. So I let them all go. I shall stay here and keep watch.”

p.src: Hearing this, Baoyu realized that here indeed was another Xiren. He smiled and said, “I’ll sit here, so you can go without worrying.” Sheyue replied, “Since you are here, there is even less reason for me to go. Wouldn’t it be nicer for the two of us to talk and joke together?” Baoyu laughed. “What shall the two of us do? It is terribly dull. Oh well—you said this morning that your scalp itched. Since we have nothing to do now, let me comb it for you with the fine-toothed comb.” “Let us do that, then,” said Sheyue. As she spoke, she brought over the dressing things and mirror case, removed her hairpins and bracelets, and let down her hair. Baoyu took up the fine-toothed comb and carefully combed it through, lock by lock. He had made only three or five strokes when Qingwen hurried in to fetch some money. The moment she saw them, she sneered, “Well! You haven’t even drunk the wedding cup together, yet already he is doing your hair!” Baoyu laughed. “Come here, and I’ll comb yours too.” “I am not blessed with such great fortune,” Qingwen replied. With that, she took the money, flung the curtain aside, and went out.

p.src: Baoyu stood behind Sheyue while she faced the mirror, and the two looked at each other in its reflection. Smiling into the mirror, Baoyu said, “She is the only one in this whole room who is forever making sharp remarks.” Hearing this, Sheyue hastily waved at him in the mirror, and Baoyu understood her meaning. Suddenly the curtain rustled, and Qingwen ran in again, demanding, “How have I been making sharp remarks? We had better settle this properly.” Sheyue laughed. “Go on with you! Why come back to question us?” Qingwen laughed. “There you go, defending him again. I know all about the secret tricks you two are playing. Wait until I win back my losses, and then we shall talk.” With that, she went straight out again. When Baoyu’s hair had been thoroughly combed, he had Sheyue quietly help him into bed, unwilling to disturb Xiren. Nothing further happened that night. When they rose early the next morning, Xiren had perspired during the night and felt somewhat relieved. She took only a little rice broth and rested quietly. Baoyu’s mind was set at ease, and after breakfast he strolled over to Aunt Xue’s quarters. It was still the first lunar month: the school was closed for the New Year holidays, while the young ladies’ quarters observed the seasonal taboo against needlework, so everyone was at leisure. Jia Huan also came over to amuse himself. He found Baochai, Xiangling, and Ying’er playing a race game with dice and counters, and wanted to join them. Baochai had always treated him just as she treated Baoyu, without showing any partiality. So when she heard that he wanted to play that day, she let him come up and sit with them. They staked ten cash on each round. Jia Huan won the first and was delighted. But after losing several rounds in succession, he began to grow anxious. In the current round it was his turn to throw the dice. A seven would give him the victory, but if he threw a six, Ying’er would need only a three on her next throw to win. He picked up the dice and threw them with all his might. One settled on five while the other spun wildly. Ying’er clapped her hands and cried, “One! One!” while Jia Huan stared wide-eyed and shouted at random, “Six—seven—eight!” But perversely enough, the die came to rest on one. Jia Huan lost his temper, snatched up the dice, and then reached for the money, claiming that he had thrown a six. Ying’er protested, “It was plainly a one!” Seeing Jia Huan grow angry, Baochai shot Ying’er a look and said, “The older you get, the less you know how to behave! Do you suppose a young master would cheat you? Put the money down at once!” Ying’er felt deeply wronged, but since Baochai had spoken, she dared not answer back. She had no choice but to put down the money, muttering, “A young master, cheating us out of these few coins, and treating even me as if I were beneath notice! The other day, when I played with Second Master Baoyu, he lost all that money without getting angry in the least. When the little maids scrambled for the money that remained, he merely laughed and let the matter pass.” Before she could finish, Baochai hastily silenced her with a sharp rebuke. Jia Huan said, “How could I ever compare with Baoyu? You are all afraid of him and friendly with him, while you bully me because I was not born to the Mistress.”

p.src: With that, he burst into tears. Baochai hurriedly consoled him. “Dear brother, don’t say such things. People will laugh at you.” Then she scolded Ying’er again. Just then Baoyu came in. Seeing them in this state, he asked what had happened. Jia Huan did not dare utter a word. Baochai had always known the rule in his family: younger brothers were all afraid of their elder brothers. But she did not know that Baoyu had no wish to be feared. He reasoned, “All my brothers have parents to discipline them. Why should I meddle and only make us less close? Besides, I am legitimate and he is a concubine’s son. Even as things stand, people gossip behind our backs; how much worse would it be if I tried to rule over him?” He also cherished another foolish notion. And what foolish notion was that? From childhood he had grown up amid a throng of girls: his own sisters Yuanchun and Tanchun; his cousins Yingchun and Xichun; and among his other relations Shi Xiangyun, Lin Daiyu, Xue Baochai, and many more. He had therefore concluded that, although human beings were born the most spiritual of all creatures, the purest essence of mountains, rivers, sun, and moon was concentrated only in girls, while bearded men were no more than dregs and muddy froth. With this foolish idea lodged in his mind, he regarded all men as coarse, muddied creatures whose existence mattered little. Only in the case of fathers, uncles, elder brothers, and younger brothers— since Confucius, the foremost sage of all antiquity, had laid down the rule— he could not defy or slight them, and so had no choice but to obey that teaching. Thus, between brothers he observed only the broadest demands of affection and propriety; it never occurred to him that, as a man, he ought to set an example for his younger kinsmen. Consequently Jia Huan and the others were not afraid of him; they yielded to him somewhat only because they feared Grandmother Jia. Now Baochai feared that Baoyu might discipline Jia Huan and make matters awkward, so she hastened to cover for him. Baoyu said, “Why cry during the first month of the New Year? If you are not happy here, go and amuse yourself somewhere else. You study every day, yet it seems your books have only muddled your head. If one thing is no good but another is good, you simply put aside the first and choose the other. Can sitting beside the thing and crying over it possibly make it better? You came here to enjoy yourself. If you cannot enjoy yourself here, go elsewhere and find some amusement. Does crying for a while count as enjoyment? You are only bringing trouble on yourself. You had better leave at once.” Hearing this, Jia Huan had no choice but to go back.

p.src: Seeing him in this state, Concubine Zhao asked, “Where have you been made someone’s kicking block this time?” When her first question met with no answer, she asked again, and Jia Huan said, “I was playing with Cousin Baochai. Ying’er bullied me and cheated me of my money, and Brother Baoyu drove me away.” Concubine Zhao spat contemptuously. “Who told you to aspire to such exalted company? You shameless, lowborn wretch! Were there no other places where you could play? Who told you to run there and invite humiliation?” As she was speaking, Xifeng happened to pass outside the window. She heard every word. She called through the window, “What is all this about, in the very first month of the New Year? Brother Huan is only a child. If he has made the slightest mistake, just instruct him. What is the use of saying such spiteful things? Whatever he does, his mother and father are there to govern him. Yet you spit abuse at him so freely! He is a master of this house. If he misbehaves, there are people responsible for teaching him. What business is it of yours? Brother Huan, come out and play with me.” Jia Huan habitually feared Xifeng even more than he feared Lady Wang. Hearing her call, he hurried out, murmuring assent. Concubine Zhao did not dare make a sound either. Xifeng said to Jia Huan, “You are a truly spineless creature! I am forever telling you: if you want to eat, drink, play, or laugh, then whichever sister, cousin, brother, or sister-in-law you like, go and enjoy yourself with that person. But you refuse to listen to me and instead let these people fill you with crooked, wicked notions and teach you sly, domineering ways. You lower yourself, choose the meanest company, and harbor malicious thoughts, yet you keep complaining that others are partial. How much money did you lose? And just look at the state you are in!” Forced to answer, Jia Huan stammered meekly, “One or two hundred cash.” Xifeng said, “A fine young master you are, carrying on like this over one or two hundred cash!” Turning to Feng’er, she ordered, “Go and fetch a string of cash. The girls are all playing in the back rooms, so take him there to join them. And you—if you behave in this low, sly way again tomorrow, I shall beat you first, then send word to the school and have them flay the skin off you! Your disgraceful conduct makes your brother itch to thrash you. If I had not restrained him, he would have kicked you in the chest hard enough to send your guts flying out.” Then she commanded sharply, “Off you go!” Jia Huan meekly followed Feng’er, received the money, and went off to play with Yingchun and the others. There is no more to be said of that.

u.src: Seeing him in this state, Concubine Zhao asked, “Where have you been made someone’s kicking block this time?”
When her first question met with no answer, she asked again, and Jia Huan said, “I was playing with Cousin Baochai. Ying’er bullied me and cheated me of my money, and Brother Baoyu drove me away.”
Concubine Zhao spat contemptuously. “Who told you to aspire to such exalted company?
You shameless, lowborn wretch!
Were there no other places where you could play?
Who told you to run there and invite humiliation?”
As she was speaking, Xifeng happened to pass outside the window.

p.src: Meanwhile, Baoyu was laughing and joking with Baochai when someone suddenly announced, “Miss Shi has arrived.” At this, Baoyu immediately rose to leave. Baochai laughed. “Wait. Let us go together and see her.” With that, she stepped down from the kang, and she and Baoyu went together to Grandmother Jia’s apartments. There was Shi Xiangyun, talking and laughing at the top of her voice. When she saw the two of them arrive, she hastened to exchange greetings with them. Lin Daiyu happened to be beside her and asked Baoyu, “Where have you been?” Baoyu replied, “At Cousin Baochai’s.” Daiyu sneered. “So that explains it. Fortunately you were detained there; otherwise you would have flown here long ago.” Baoyu laughed. “Am I allowed only to play with you and relieve your boredom? I merely paid her an occasional visit, and already you say such things.” Lin Daiyu said, “What a ridiculous thing to say! Whether you go or not is none of my concern. I never asked you to relieve my boredom. You are perfectly welcome never to speak to me again!” With that, she went back to her room in a huff.

p.src: Baoyu hurried after her and asked, “Why are you angry again when everything was perfectly fine? Even if I said something wrong, you could at least have stayed there awhile and talked and laughed with the others. Instead, you have come away to sulk by yourself.” “What business is it of yours?” said Lin Daiyu. Baoyu laughed. “Of course I would never dare to govern you. But I cannot simply stand by and watch you ruin your health.” “If I ruin my health and die, what has that to do with you?” said Lin Daiyu. Baoyu said, “Why talk of dying and living during the New Year festivities?” “I insist on talking of death!” said Lin Daiyu. “I shall die this very moment! You are afraid of death, so may you live to be a hundred. How does that suit you?” Baoyu laughed. “If this quarrelling is to go on and on, do you think I would still fear death? I would be better off dead and done with it.” Daiyu quickly replied, “Exactly! If things are to go on like this, I would be better off dead and done with it.” Baoyu said, “I said that I would be better off dead. Do not mishear me and then blame me for it.” As they were speaking, Baochai came over and said, “Cousin Shi is waiting for you.” With that, she pushed Baoyu away with her. Left there, Daiyu grew still more heartsick and stood weeping by the window.

p.src: Before the time needed to drink two cups of tea had passed, Baoyu returned. At the sight of him, Lin Daiyu sobbed all the harder and could not stop crying. Seeing her like this, Baoyu knew how difficult it would be to win her around and marshalled a thousand tender, soothing words to comfort her. But before he could open his mouth, Daiyu spoke first: “What have you come back for? You have someone to amuse yourself with now—someone who can recite better than I, compose better, write better, and laugh and talk better; someone who was afraid you might be angry and pulled you away. Why have you come back here? Just leave me to live or die as I please!” Hearing this, Baoyu hurried close and said softly, “You are such an intelligent person. Can it be that you have never heard, ‘The close should not be estranged for the sake of the distant, nor the earlier displaced by the later’? Confused as I may be, I understand those two principles. First, you and I are first cousins through my father and your mother, while Cousin Bao and I are first cousins through our mothers; in kinship she is more distant from me than you are. Second, you came here first. The two of us have eaten at the same table and slept in the same bed while growing up to this age, whereas she has only just arrived. How could I possibly grow distant from you for her sake?” Lin Daiyu spat in disdain. “Do you think I want you to distance yourself from her? What sort of person would that make me? What concerns me is my own heart.” Baoyu said, “What concerns me is my heart too. Can it be that you understand your own heart but not mine?” At this Lin Daiyu lowered her head and said nothing. After a long pause, she said, “You are forever blaming people for taking offence at you, yet you never realize how much you yourself provoke and torment them. Take today’s weather: it is plainly bitterly cold, so why did you go and take off your grey-squirrel cloak?” Baoyu laughed. “Of course I was wearing it. When I saw you angry, I grew hot-headed and took it off.” Lin Daiyu sighed. “When you catch cold later, you will be hungry as well and start clamouring for food again.”

p.src: As the two were speaking, Xiangyun came over and said with a laugh, “Second Cousin, Cousin Lin, you two play together every day. I have had such trouble getting here, yet neither of you pays the least attention to me.” Daiyu laughed. “What a chatterbox you are for someone with a lisp! You cannot even pronounce the word ‘second’ in ‘Second Cousin,’ but keep calling him ‘Love Cousin, Love Cousin.’ Next time we play the encirclement game, you will be calling out ‘one, love, three, four, five’ again.” Baoyu laughed. “If you keep imitating her, you will soon develop a lisp yourself.” Shi Xiangyun said, “She never spares anyone in the least and does nothing but pick at people’s faults. Even if you are better than everyone else in the world, you still need not make fun of every person you meet. I shall name one person: if you dare find fault with her, I will admit defeat.” Daiyu quickly asked who it was. Xiangyun said, “If you dare pick out Cousin Bao’s faults, I will grant that you are truly remarkable. I admit I am not your equal, but in what way is she inferior to you?” Daiyu gave a cold laugh. “I wondered whom you meant, and it turns out to be her! How would I dare find fault with her?” Before she could finish, Baoyu hurriedly changed the subject. Xiangyun laughed. “Naturally, I shall never be your match as long as I live. I only pray that one day you will get a lisping husband, Cousin Lin, so that from morning till night you may listen to him saying ‘love’ and ‘ugh.’ Amitabha Buddha! Then I shall have had my revenge before my very eyes!” Everyone burst out laughing at this, and Xiangyun promptly turned and ran away. To learn what happened next, read the following chapter.
